task.description: Rework docs/agents/design/REQ-038.md to fix the single blocking FAIL from step-01b: the design never stated how hasPastCheckIn's result reaches decideRegistrationOutcome's required inviteSatisfied field on the plain (no-code) registration path, and registerForEvent (the function that actually builds RegistrationDecisionInput and calls decideRegistrationOutcome for that path) was absent from the file-change manifest. Read apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's full, current registerForEvent (lines 119-263) to ground the fix in its real transaction/lock shape before editing the design doc.

result.summary: Fixed the one blocking gap. Chose option (b): hasPastCheckIn is called from inside registerForEvent's own existing transaction (using the already-open tx handle and the already-available userId parameter), as a new internal step inserted between registerForEvent's existing step 2 (event lock, which yields event.requiresInvite) and its existing step 6 (the decideRegistrationOutcome call, which now receives the computed value as the new inviteSatisfied field). registerForEvent's external signature (db, userId, eventId, evaluationTime) is unchanged, so handlers/registration.ts's existing register:<eventId> callback call site needs no edit. Option (a) (handler computes hasPastCheckIn before calling registerForEvent, passed in as a new parameter) was considered and rejected in the doc for two independent reasons: (1) it would read the invite-satisfaction input outside the transaction that makes the admission decision and performs the write, unlike every other input to that same decision (existingAdmission, admittedCount/seatsLeft, event.status), introducing a real TOCTOU gap where today there is none; (2) it would be inconsistent with this same design's own established atomicity discipline elsewhere (redemption path §3.1 step 5's 'never trust a pre-tx read', invite_codes locked fresh inside the transaction rather than reused from an outside pre-check).
changes: Top-of-document 'Files this design expects to change' list: registerForEvent explicitly named as gaining a new internal step inside its existing transaction (no signature/external-caller change), alongside its already-listed changes (decideRegistrationOutcome branch, hasPastCheckIn read, redemption entry point).

SS2.2 'Where it's called' rewritten: states the resolved option (b) explicitly, quotes the current registerForEvent line numbers (126-188, specifically requiresInvite: event.requiresInvite at line 181) it is grounded in, states the exact insertion point (after existing step 2, before existing step 6), states the exact economy-note gating (query only when event.requiresInvite is true, else inviteSatisfied: false unconditionally), and states this is the only call site for hasPastCheckIn (the redemption path never calls it; it always passes inviteSatisfied: true by construction once a code validates).
SS8 AC7 row updated to cite SS2.2's exact call-site resolution alongside the existing SS2/SS1.1/SS1.2 references.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for re-gate. Every other item already passed step-01b's review (FR-4 resolution, identity-leakage reasoning, atomic used_count increment, decideRegistrationOutcome minimal-diff claim, hasPastCheckIn purity, consent-gate reuse) and was not touched in this rework.
